title: Resource-domain authorization matrix and guard-tiering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a domain-oriented RBAC v2 role model that supports hierarchical resources, scoped permissions, temporal elevation, and guard-tiered admin controls. This ticket captures the authorization matrix at the resource-domain level (domains, projects, model deployments, dedicated pools), the scope definitions consumed by the policy evaluation engine, and the operational guard tiers for admin actions. The output is a canonical permissions matrix, migration steps from RBAC v1, audit logging contract, and SAML/SSO attribute mapping guidance.
background: Current RBAC is coarse-grained: organization-level roles and a flat permission list. As customers adopt Dedicated and Private, they need predictable, tenant-scoped permissions and fine-grained admin controls (e.g., deny-create-pool vs. allow-manage-pool). Previous investigations (ENG-4721, ENG-74182) highlighted ambiguity around resource boundaries and temporal elevation. This work unblocks Dedicated onboarding, Private compliance, and fine-grained console controls.
goals: Define resource-domain taxonomy and canonical object paths (org, domain, project, deployment, runtime-pool)
Specify a permissions matrix mapping actions to role templates and scopes (read, write, manage, audit) for each resource class
Design guard-tiering for admin-sensitive actions (breakglass, approver workflows, require-2fa) and map to temporal elevation flows
Surface audit logging contract: what events, fields, immutable context, and retention labeling are required
Provide SAML attribute mapping guidance to convert IdP groups/roles into domain-scoped RBAC bindings
Produce migration plan from RBAC v1 to v2 with tooling to validate and backfill bindings
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Chosen domain-first taxonomy instead of resource-first to reduce cross-tenant policy complexity
2025-02-24: Adopt 'scope-centric' permission strings (e.g., model.deploy:create, pool.manage:scale) rather than RPC verbs to improve policy expressivity
2025-02-28: Guard-tiering will use three tiers (standard admin, elevated admin, breakglass) with different audit hooks and TTLs
2025-03-01: Temporal elevation will rely on short-lived elevation tokens with 15-minute default TTL and optional MFA enforcement for sensitive tiers
2025-03-02: Audit log schema v2 chosen to include actor_id, actor_roles_at_time, resource_path, action, outcome, request_context_hash
tradeoffs: We prioritize predictable least-privilege boundaries which increases the complexity of role bindings and the migration burden. Opting for scope-centric permission strings costs us an initial increase in policy enforcement surface area but yields clearer mapping across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. The TTL for elevation is conservative (15m) to reduce blast radius; shorter TTL increases UX friction for long admin tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical resource taxonomy doc published and reviewed by Security/Compliance
Permissions matrix covers all console and API actions and is validated by the policy engine tests
Migration tool can simulate policy equivalence and backfill 90% of widely used bindings in staging
Audit logging contract implemented and tested end-to-end in staging with sample events captured in the Console with per-action cost metadata
SAML mapping pattern documented with example IdP rules and a reference mapping script
tasks: Draft resource taxonomy and canonical paths (Aisha)
Enumerate API and console actions and map to scopes (Marco)
Prototype permission strings and integrate with policy evaluator (Eng-Policy Team)
Implement audit log schema changes and event hooks (Infra/Logging)
Create SAML attribute mapping examples and test with Okta and ADFS (SRE/SSO)
Build migration tool to analyze and propose role translations (Tools)
Run canary migration for 2 customer orgs in staging and gather telemetry
implementation_notes: Policy evaluator will accept scope strings in the format <resource_class>.<action>:<modifier> where resource_class is one of org|domain|project|deployment|pool. Bindings are tuples (principal, role_template, resource_path). Role templates are parameterized with scope_filters and allowed-time-windows. For breakglass, the system will emit an 'elevation_request' event and create a short-lived credential tied to the requesting actor and reason. All admin-sensitive actions must log pre- and post-state snapshots in the audit event. Implementation to follow feature flag 'rbac_v2_domain_mode' for safe rollout.
migration_strategy: Phase 1: Publish matrix and run simulation mode where policy-evaluator provides deny/allow predictions for existing bindings. Phase 2: Run automated translation for common role names and surface edge cases for manual review. Phase 3: Canary cutover for two staging orgs followed by opt-in migration for customers. Provide a rollback tool that re-applies previous RBAC v1 bindings. All migrations will be logged and observable.
rollback_plan: Feature flag off: rbac_v2_domain_mode toggled to false will stop evaluating new v2 bindings and policy-evaluator returns to legacy mode. Migration tool will retain snapshots of original bindings to restore. Emergency rebind scripts available for top 10 customer roles.
audit_logging_requirements: Events must include: timestamp (ISO8601), actor_id, actor_email, actor_roles_at_time (list), resource_path, action, parameters_redacted_hash, outcome (success|failure), request_id, request_duration_ms, auth_method (sso|api-key|elevated-token). Sensitive payloads must not be logged; instead store hash and pointer to secure artifact store. Retention policy: 90 days default, 7 years for compliance flagging.
saml_mapping_notes: Recommend mapping IdP groups to domain-scoped roles using claim 'redwood_domain_bindings'. Provide sample SAML attribute mapping script that ingests groups and outputs role bindings with optional 'domain' claim. For enterprise customers wanting nested groups, support group->role flattening rules and explicit deny bindings. Provide examples for Okta (group attribute: 'groups'), Azure AD, and ADFS.
admin_controls: Introduce guard-tiering levels: standard-admin (can manage day-to-day resources), elevated-admin (requires MFA and approval for sensitive actions), breakglass (emergency single-use elevation logged and audited). Admin UI will show current active elevations, TTL, and justifications. Console actions that change billing, data export, or cryptographic keys are restricted to elevated-admin or breakglass with additional approval steps.
rollout_plan: Start in staging behind 'rbac_v2_domain_mode'. Run 2-week alpha with internal teams. After alpha, select two early-adopter customers for a limited beta. Collect compatibility telemetry, audit event completeness, and migration failure rates. Ramp to GA in 4 sprints with migration tooling enabled and docs. Provide a 30-day opt-out window for customers post-migration.
qa_plan: Unit tests for scope parsing and policy evaluation; integration tests exercising staged migration; E2E tests for elevation flows (request, grant, audit); fuzz tests for malformed resource paths; privacy tests ensuring no PII in logs. Manual QA to validate SAML mappings with Okta and Azure AD test tenants.
notes: Early engineering spike found edge cases with wildcarded resource_path resolution when combining domain-level and project-level bindings. Plan to disallow overlapping wildcard precedence; explicit precedence rules documented in taxonomy. Coordinate with Console team to surface effective permissions in user profile page.
customer_impact_notes: High-impact for Dedicated and Private customers because migration changes effective permissions. We will communicate planned changes, provide dry-run reports, and offer migration assistance.
